A.explanation: Period of $6.0\text{ cm}$ gives $f \approx 330\text{ Hz}$ and height of $3.0\text{ cm}$ from centre gives $0.6\text{ mV}$.

B.explanation: Frequency is correct but $1.2\text{ mV}$ is the peak-to-trough voltage, which is twice the amplitude.

C.explanation: Amplitude is correct but $670\text{ Hz}$ uses half a cycle for the period instead of the trough-to-trough distance.

D.explanation: Uses half the period and the full peak-to-trough height, so both frequency is doubled and voltage is doubled.

hints: Count horizontal squares between two matching points on the trace, such as trough to trough, and multiply by the $0.5\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ time-base to get the period $T$.
Recall $f = 1/T$ for the sound wave, so a period near $3.0\text{ ms}$ gives a frequency of a few hundred hertz.
Measure the vertical height from the centre line to a peak or trough, not peak to trough, and multiply by the $0.2\text{ mV cm}^{-1}$ Y-sensitivity to get amplitude.
walkthrough: Identify one full cycle on the c.r.o. screen. The distance from one trough to the next trough is $6.0\text{ cm}$ horizontally.
Convert horizontal length to period using the time-base: $T = 6.0 \times 0.5\text{ ms} = 3.0\text{ ms} = 3.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}$.
Calculate frequency: $f = 1/T = 1/(3.0 \times 10^{-3}) \approx 333\text{ Hz}$, which matches the $330\text{ Hz}$ row to sensible precision.
Find amplitude vertically. From the centre of the wave to the top of the peak or bottom of the trough is $3.0\text{ cm}$.
Convert vertical length to voltage: $V = 3.0 \times 0.2\text{ mV} = 0.6\text{ mV}$. The $6.0\text{ cm}$ peak-to-trough height would be $1.2\text{ mV}$ and is not the amplitude.
Frequency $330\text{ Hz}$ with amplitude $0.6\text{ mV}$ matches the table. This is option A
